steps.title: A census of guests who never signed the lease
steps.text: Every few nights I walk the apartment with a notebook and a phone flashlight. This scroll is a ledger of who showed up — plotted in bright wool colors, because if you must count them, count them beautifully.

steps.title: The first antennae
steps.text: It started as a single silhouette by the stove — a modest integer, almost polite. I told myself it was a traveler, not a trend.

steps.title: They learned the floor plan
steps.text: Counts climbed through February. The kitchen became a crossroads; the hallway a highway. The chart doesn't judge — it only remembers.

steps.title: Moroccan geometry, domestic chaos
steps.text: My grandmother's rugs taught me that repetition can hold disorder. Diamonds and stars frame the data the way a good border frames a wild center.

steps.title: A brief truce
steps.text: Traps, caulk, and stubborn hope. The line dips. Zero nights are the strangest — absence as data, silence as a number.

steps.title: The census continues
steps.text: The count is never really over. Update the JSON, add your photos, watch the roaches scatter as you scroll — and tell the story your kitchen deserves.
